## Summary

Roughly **8 of the 20 active features** are spurious — they are mislabeled or are artifacts (programming tokens, punctuation, unrelated fragments) that have no coherent semantic relationship to either toxicity or identity-group signals. Their activation on this input appears to be noise rather than meaningful signal. While some features legitimately capture toxicity (profanity, anti-marginalized-group rhetoric), the presence of these junk/mislabeled features means the SAE is encoding spurious patterns that could degrade interpretability of the toxicity classification. The concern about spurious identity-group encoding is **partially valid** — though more precisely, many features are spurious in a broader sense (noise/mislabeled) rather than specifically encoding identity groups incorrectly.
